records.speaker: Follower
records.source_meaning: A follower or adherent of the sect.
records.localization_note: Follower preserves 信徒 and the group’s allegiance to the Sect Leader. It fits both the collective chants and the individual map request without assigning a personal name.
records.context: The follower answers each declaration by the Sect Leader with cheers. The follower repeats the leader’s chant at the stone circle and cheers the group’s plan. The follower cheers the leader, then cries out as the group is captured. A follower interrupts the guildmaster to ask for a map, which connects the sect to the ruined site. The follower echoes the Sect Leader as the ritual escalates and the villagers intervene. The follower cheers the Sect Leader and flees from what they mistake for the army.

records.speaker: Francisca
records.source_meaning: The personal name フランシスカ.
records.localization_note: Thanks Rafael for returning the Frozen Rose and tells him about a church. Francisca represents フランシスカ and fits her existing greeting and portrait.
records.context: Thanks Rafael for returning the Frozen Rose and tells him about a church

records.speaker: Marie
records.source_meaning: The personal name マリー.
records.localization_note: Welcomes Rafael and shares her customers’ theories about the ruins. Marie preserves マリー without changing the host’s identity to Maria.
records.context: Welcomes Rafael and shares her customers’ theories about the ruins

records.speaker: Margrete
records.source_meaning: The personal name マルグレーテ.
records.localization_note: Offers a contact at a nearby church after hearing about the treasure hunt. Keep the existing Margrete spelling for マルグレーテ.
records.context: Offers a contact at a nearby church after hearing about the treasure hunt

records.speaker: Wanda
records.source_meaning: The personal name ワンダ.
records.localization_note: Greets the player and says she knows of no famous ruins in town. Wanda retains ワンダ and the direct personal name.
records.context: Greets the player and says she knows of no famous ruins in town

records.speaker: Julia
records.source_meaning: The personal name ジュリア.
records.localization_note: Greets the player and considers the question before answering about the local ruins. Julia is the established form of ジュリア.
records.context: Greets the player and considers the question before answering about the local ruins

records.speaker: Donna
records.source_meaning: The personal name ドナ.
records.localization_note: Recommends visiting Santiago Cathedral while the party is in Seville. Donna retains ドナ as her name without adding a social title.
records.context: Recommends visiting Santiago Cathedral while the party is in Seville

records.speaker: Matilda
records.source_meaning: The personal name マチルダ.
records.localization_note: Alerts the party to the Colosseum and reminds them to buy a map. Matilda is the established form of マチルダ.
records.context: Alerts the party to the Colosseum and reminds them to buy a map

records.speaker: Myrine
records.source_meaning: The personal name ミュリネー.
records.localization_note: Points out the ruins on a hill above town. Keep the established spelling of ミュリネー without tying her to a historical or mythological namesake.
records.context: Points out the ruins on a hill above town

records.speaker: Faticia
records.source_meaning: The personal name ファティシア.
records.localization_note: Teases Hodram and passes on a rumor about a hidden Christian village. Keep the existing rendering of ファティシア, also used in the registered tavern exchange.
records.context: Teases Hodram and passes on a rumor about a hidden Christian village

records.speaker: Nelly
records.source_meaning: The personal name ネリー.
records.localization_note: Insists Rafael see the pyramid and offers directions. Nelly retains ネリー and the separate Alexandria name-panel label.
records.context: Insists Rafael see the pyramid and offers directions

records.speaker: Hatra
records.source_meaning: The personal name ハトラ.
records.localization_note: Uses the good weather to suggest a visit to rumored ruins. Keep the established Hatra for ハトラ without treating the name as a geographic claim.
records.context: Uses the good weather to suggest a visit to rumored ruins

records.speaker: Safia
records.source_meaning: The personal name サフィア.
records.localization_note: Thanks Rafael for helping her dance and offers a lead on a mosque. Safia retains サフィア and keeps the greeting personal.
records.context: Thanks Rafael for helping her dance and offers a lead on a mosque

records.speaker: Benazir
records.source_meaning: The personal name ベナジール.
records.localization_note: Repays the player’s gift with a tip about a site requiring a map. Benazir retains ベナジール without adding a title or surname.
records.context: Repays the player’s gift with a tip about a site requiring a map

records.speaker: Lucia
records.source_meaning: The personal name ルシア.
records.localization_note: Warns the party about the forest and offers directions if they bring a map. Lucia retains ルシア as the personal name used in this exchange.
records.context: Warns the party about the forest and offers directions if they bring a map

records.speaker: Titis
records.source_meaning: The personal name ティティス.
records.localization_note: Makes an exception for the travelers when she tells them about nearby ruins. Keep the project spelling of ティティス and its separate Jakarta catalogue label.
records.context: Makes an exception for the travelers when she tells them about nearby ruins

records.speaker: Mihwa
records.source_meaning: The personal name 美華.
records.localization_note: Quietly shares directions to the city gate despite restrictions on visitors. The clean field gives 美華 without a reading. Keep the existing project reading without inferring nationality from it.
records.context: Quietly shares directions to the city gate despite restrictions on visitors

records.speaker: Reika
records.source_meaning: The personal name 麗姫.
records.localization_note: Tells Rafael and Claudio what she heard about the crown and the earlier visitor. The clean field gives 麗姫 without a reading. Keep the project reading and leave the visitor’s identity tentative.
records.context: Tells Rafael and Claudio what she heard about the crown and the earlier visitor

records.speaker: Sakura
records.source_meaning: The personal name さくら.
records.localization_note: Listens to Rafael’s travel story and asks about chintz. Sakura preserves the source さくら as her given name.
records.context: Listens to Rafael’s travel story and asks about chintz

records.speaker: Verisa
records.source_meaning: The personal name ヴェリーサ.
records.localization_note: Uses her improved fortune-telling to thank Rafael and point him toward ruins. Keep the project spelling of ヴェリーサ and its separate Sao Jorge label.
records.context: Uses her improved fortune-telling to thank Rafael and point him toward ruins

records.speaker: Silvia
records.source_meaning: The personal name シルビア.
records.localization_note: Shares a report of an illustrated map but cannot say where it is. Silvia retains シルビア with no extra surname.
records.context: Shares a report of an illustrated map but cannot say where it is

records.speaker: Isabel
records.source_meaning: The personal name イサベル.
records.localization_note: Asks the crew to inquire about a missing monk. Isabel retains イサベル and the Japanese distinction between her Bahamas label and the Havana port name.
records.context: Asks the crew to inquire about a missing monk

SC0 B115.summary: The follower answers each declaration by the Sect Leader with cheers.

speeches.Japanese: すげえ古そうな遺跡だったな
speeches.English: Those ruins looked really ancient.

speeches.Japanese:
それにしても、奴らは何者なんだろう
生け贄なんてかなり野蛮だよ…
speeches.English:
Who were those people, anyway? 
 Sacrifices... That's barbaric.

speeches.Japanese:
あいつら、絶対、まともじゃねえよ！
だが…
またここに集まるって言ってたな
speeches.English:
They're out of their minds! But... 
 they said they'd be back, right?

speeches.Japanese:
彼ら、いったい何を
するつもりなんだろう？
speeches.English: What are they planning?

speeches.Japanese:
さあな
そういや、『お告げの日の前夜』と
か言ってたな
それっていつなんだ？
speeches.English:
Beats me. Oh yeah, they said 
 something about 'the night before
 the day of revelation.' When's 
 that supposed to be?

speeches.Japanese:
…ほら、あのおまじないの文句
『光と闇が拮抗するとき』っていうのが
その日のことなんじゃない？
speeches.English:
...Remember that incantation? 'When
 light and darkness are evenly
 matched.' Could that be the day
 they mean?

speeches.Japanese:
はあ？
それだけじゃさっぱり分かんねえぞ
speeches.English: Huh? That tells us nothing.

speeches.Japanese:
とにかく、何か手を考えよう
生け贄なんて、やめさせなきゃ！
speeches.English:
Anyway, let's come up with a plan. 
 We have to stop the sacrifices!

speeches.Japanese: あああ～～～…
speeches.English: Aaaah...

speeches.Japanese: おおお～～～！
speeches.English: Ooooh!

speeches.Japanese:
これは、お告げなのだ！
我々『古代巨石文明研究会』は
近く、世界を制圧するであろう！
speeches.English:
This is a divine revelation! 
 We, the Ancient Megalithic 
 Civilization Research Society, 
 shall soon conquer the world!

speeches.Japanese:
我々は選ばれし者！
ここに書かれた宝物を掘り出し
神をもおそれぬ愚民どもを
支配するのだ！！
speeches.English:
We are the chosen ones!
 We shall unearth the treasure
 described here and rule
 those ignorant fools 
 who show no fear of the divine!

speeches.Japanese: おおーっ！
speeches.English: Ooooh!

speeches.Japanese:
まず手始めに、この村を襲う！
我々をばかにした連中に
思い知らせてやるのだ！
speeches.English:
First, we attack this village! 
 We'll teach those who mocked us
 a lesson!

speeches.Japanese: おおおーっ！！
speeches.English: Ooooh!

SC0 B293.summary: The follower repeats the leader’s chant at the stone circle and cheers the group’s plan.

speeches.Japanese: 気をつけて進もう
speeches.English: Let's go carefully.

speeches.Japanese: 危ないっ！
speeches.English: Look out!

speeches.Japanese: 撃って！
speeches.English: Shoot!

speeches.Japanese: 水夫が少し負傷したようです
speeches.English:
Some of your sailors seem
 to have suffered minor injuries.

speeches.Japanese: しっ、がまんして
speeches.English: Shh. Hold on a little longer.

speeches.Japanese: エミリオ？
speeches.English: Emilio?

speeches.Japanese: すう…
speeches.English: Zzz...

speeches.Japanese:
“振り”じゃなくて
本当に寝ちゃってる…
speeches.English:
He wasn't pretending. He actually
 fell asleep...

speeches.Japanese: １日経過しました
speeches.English: One day passed.

speeches.Japanese:
まずいよ、提督！
あいつ、人食いグマかもよ！？
下手に手を出すと
こっちが危ないって！！
speeches.English:
This is bad, Admiral! That bear
 might be a man-eater! If we go 
 after it, we're the ones who'll
 be in trouble!

speeches.Japanese:
水夫の疲労がだいぶ上がりました
負傷者がでたようです
speeches.English:
Your sailors are considerably
 more fatigued. Some seem 
 to have been injured.

speeches.Japanese: 逃げよう！！
speeches.English: Run!

speeches.Japanese:
あれかな？
変な人たちの集まりっていうのは？
speeches.English:
Is that them? The strange group
 we heard about?

speeches.Japanese: あああ～～～…
speeches.English: Aaaah...

speeches.Japanese: おおお～～～！
speeches.English: Ooooh!

speeches.Japanese:
う、歌？
なんか危ねえ雰囲気だぞ
speeches.English:
S-singing? Something about 
 this feels wrong.

speeches.Japanese:
日は巡り、月は巡り、星は巡る
光と闇が拮抗するとき
其れもまた光と闇の狭間に在り
speeches.English:
Round goes the sun, round goes 
 the moon, round go the stars.
 When light and darkness
 stand in balance,
 it too lies between light
 and darkness.

speeches.Japanese:
日は巡り、月は巡り、星は巡る
光と闇が拮抗するとき
其れもまた光と闇の狭間に在り
speeches.English:
Round goes the sun, round goes 
 the moon, round go the stars.
 When light and darkness
 stand in balance,
 it too lies between light
 and darkness.

speeches.Japanese:
ヤツら、何言ってやがんだ？
まじないか？
speeches.English:
What the hell are they saying? 
 Is that some kind of spell?

speeches.Japanese:
我々『古代巨石文明研究会』が
神託を手にするときは近づいている！
そして、いよいよ世界制圧の野望を
実現するのだ！
speeches.English:
The time is nearly upon us!
 We of the Ancient Megalithic 
 Civilization Research Society
 will receive the divine message
 and at last fulfill our ambition 
 to rule the world!

speeches.Japanese:
お告げの日の前夜より、再び祈りを
捧げる！
我々を侮辱した、愚かなる輩を
生け贄に捧げるのだ！
speeches.English:
We will begin our prayers again
 on the eve of the revelation!
 The fools who insulted us
 shall be our sacrifice!

speeches.Japanese: おおう！
speeches.English: Ooh!

speeches.Japanese: 世界制圧！？
speeches.English: Rule the world?!

speeches.Japanese:
生け贄だあ？
マジかよ、こいつら！？
speeches.English:
Sacrifice?!
 Are these people serious?!

speeches.Japanese:
それまでは巨石に近づかぬように！
本日は、これにて解散する！
speeches.English:
Until then, stay away
 from the great stones! 
 We are dismissed for today!

speeches.Japanese: 行っちゃった
speeches.English: They're gone.

speeches.Japanese: 行ってみようぜ
speeches.English: Let's go take a look.

SC0 B253.summary: Thanks Rafael for returning the Frozen Rose and tells him about a church

speeches.Japanese: あ、いらっしゃい！
speeches.English: Oh, welcome back!

speeches.Japanese: 盗まれたバラの置物って、これ？
speeches.English:
Is this the rose ornament
 that was stolen?

speeches.Japanese:
あっ！？
見つけてくれたのね！！
ありがとうっ！！
speeches.English: Oh! You found it! Thank you so much!

speeches.Japanese: 凍てついたバラを渡しました
speeches.English: You handed over the Frozen Rose.

speeches.Japanese:
もうダメだと思っていたのに
本当に見つかるなんて…
あなたのおかげね♪
speeches.English:
I thought I'd never see it again.
 I can't believe you really 
 found it... It's all thanks to you!

speeches.Japanese:
喜んでくれて、僕もうれしいよ
それじゃ
speeches.English:
I'm glad you're happy. Well, I'd 
 better be going.

speeches.Japanese: あっ、待って
speeches.English: Oh, wait!

speeches.Japanese:
あなたたち、世界各地を
探検しているんでしょう？
speeches.English:
You and your crew explore places 
 all over the world, don't you?

speeches.Japanese:
この街の郊外に、木造の教会があるわ
ヨーロッパでは珍しい建築なの
よかったら訪ねてみて
speeches.English:
There's a wooden church just 
 outside town. You don't see many 
 buildings like it in Europe. You 
 should visit if you get the chance.

speeches.Japanese:
ありがとう
行ってみることにするよ
speeches.English: Thanks. I'll go take a look.

speeches.Japanese:
本当にありがとう！
また、来てね！
speeches.English:
Thank you again! Come back 
 and see me!

SC0 B297.summary: Welcomes Rafael and shares her customers’ theories about the ruins

speeches.Japanese: あら、いらっしゃい
speeches.English: Oh, welcome!

speeches.Japanese: あの遺跡のことについて知りたいの？
speeches.English: Want to know about those ruins?

speeches.Japanese:
お客さんの話では
暦や時間を測定するために、使われた
という説があるらしいわよ
speeches.English:
Some of my customers say the ruins 
 might have been used to keep 
 a calendar and tell the time.

speeches.Japanese: 暦や時間を…
speeches.English: A calendar and a way to tell time...

SC0 B109.summary: Offers a contact at a nearby church after hearing about the treasure hunt

speeches.Japanese:
ねえ。ちょっと小耳に挟んだんだけど
あなたたち、世界中に散らばってる
なんだか不思議な宝物を探して
いるんですって？
speeches.English:
Hey, I heard you're hunting
 for some mysterious treasures
 scattered all over the world.
 Is that true?

speeches.Japanese:
この近くにある教会の神父さんは
とっても物知りなの。役に立つお話を
伺えるかもしれないわよ
speeches.English:
The priest at the church nearby
 knows all sorts of things. 
 You might hear something useful
 if you talk to him.

SC0 B264.summary: Greets the player and says she knows of no famous ruins in town

speeches.Japanese: あら、FIさん
speeches.English: Oh, FI!

speeches.Japanese:
えっ？　世界中の遺跡を探してる？
残念だけど…この街には
特に有名な遺跡はないのよ
speeches.English:
You're looking for ruins 
 all over the world? I'm afraid 
 there aren't any especially
 famous ones here.

SC0 B263.summary: Greets the player and considers the question before answering about the local ruins

speeches.Japanese:
FIさん
いらっしゃい
speeches.English: Welcome, FI.

speeches.Japanese:
えっ？　世界中の遺跡を探してるの？
うーん、そうねえ。この街には
特に有名な遺跡はないわね
speeches.English:
Oh? You're looking for ruins 
 all over the world? Hmm, let's 
 see... There aren't any especially 
 famous ones in this town.

SC0 B111.summary: Recommends visiting Santiago Cathedral while the party is in Seville

speeches.Japanese:
ちょっと待って
あなたたち、サン＝チャゴ大聖堂に
行ったことはある？
speeches.English:
Wait. Have you visited 
 Santiago Cathedral?
Hm?

speeches.Japanese:
昔からヨーロッパ中の人々が
巡礼に訪れているの
けっこう有名な場所なのよ
speeches.English:
People from all over Europe
 have been making pilgrimages there 
 for ages. It's quite famous.

speeches.Japanese:
セビリアに来たついでに
一度行ってきたら？
道を教えてあげるわ
speeches.English:
Since you're in Seville, 
 why not visit it? I'll give
 you directions.

SC0 B311.summary: Alerts the party to the Colosseum and reminds them to buy a map

speeches.Japanese:
あ、FIさん
いいところに来た
speeches.English:
Oh, FI! You've come
 at just the right time.

speeches.Japanese: あなた、コロッセウムって知ってる？
speeches.English: Have you heard of the Colosseum?

speeches.Japanese: コロッセウム？
speeches.English: The Colosseum?

speeches.Japanese:
ローマ時代の遺跡よ
あなたが遺跡を探してるって聞いたから
教えてあげようと思って
speeches.English:
It's a ruin from Roman times.
 I heard you were looking 
 for places like that, so I thought 
 I'd tell you about it.

speeches.Japanese:
ありがとう、助かるよ
ようし、行ってみよう
speeches.English: Thanks, that helps. Let's go see it.

speeches.Japanese:
ええ、気をつけて
地図を買うのを忘れずにね
speeches.English: Take care. Remember to buy a map.

SC0 B257.summary: Points out the ruins on a hill above town

speeches.Japanese: あら、FIさん
speeches.English: Hello, FI.

speeches.Japanese:
あなたも古代文明に興味があるの？
この街にも遺跡があるのよ
speeches.English:
Are you interested in ancient
 civilizations, too? We have some 
 ruins right here in town.

speeches.Japanese:
知らなかったでしょ？
でもすぐ近くなのよ。ほら
ここから見える丘の上がそうなの
speeches.English:
You didn't know? They're close 
 by. See that hill? The ruins 
 are right on top.

SC0 B258.summary: Insists Rafael see the pyramid and offers directions

speeches.Japanese: ねえ、ピラミッドにはもう行った？
speeches.English: Have you seen the pyramid yet?

speeches.Japanese: ううん、まだだけど
speeches.English: No, not yet.

speeches.Japanese:
この街に来たなら
一度は見てかなきゃ
道を教えてあげるから、ね？
行ってらっしゃいよ
speeches.English:
You've come all this way.
 You have to see it at least once!
 I'll tell you how to get there,
 all right? Go take a look!

speeches.Japanese: う、うん
speeches.English: O-okay.

SC0 B259.summary: Uses the good weather to suggest a visit to rumored ruins

speeches.Japanese:
いらっしゃい
FIさん
今日も過ごしやすいお天気ね
speeches.English:
Welcome, FI! It's lovely out 
 again today, isn't it?

speeches.Japanese:
そうそう。あなた、この街の近くの
遺跡に行ったことある？
ソロモン王の宝物庫だったって
噂もあるのよ
speeches.English:
Oh, have you been to the ruins near
 town? Some say they were King
 Solomon's treasury.

speeches.Japanese: へえ
speeches.English: Oh, really?

speeches.Japanese:
今日なんて絶好のピクニック日和だし
ちょっと出かけてみたらどう？
speeches.English:
It's perfect weather for a picnic
 today. Why not go out
 and take a look?

SC0 B314.summary: Thanks Rafael for helping her dance and offers a lead on a mosque

speeches.Japanese:
あら、FIさん
いらっしゃい！
speeches.English: Oh, FI! Welcome!

speeches.Japanese:
あなたのおかげで、とっても踊りが
うまくなったのよ！
speeches.English:
Thanks to you, my dancing's gotten 
 so much better!

speeches.Japanese: 本当？　よかったね！
speeches.English: Really? Great!

speeches.Japanese: お礼にいいこと教えてあげる
speeches.English:
I've got something to tell 
 you, as a thank-you.

speeches.Japanese:
この街のずっと内陸に昔の王様を
まつったモスクがあるんだけど
とってもステキな宝物があるんですって
speeches.English:
A mosque far inland honors 
 a king from long ago.
 They say it holds quite a treasure.

speeches.Japanese:
王様に認められた人だけが、その宝物を
手に入れられるって噂なの
試しに行ってみたら？
speeches.English:
They say only someone the king 
 finds worthy can get the treasure. 
 Why don't you give it a try?

SC0 B124.summary: Repays the player’s gift with a tip about a site requiring a map

speeches.Japanese: ねえ、待って
speeches.English: Hey, wait.

speeches.Japanese:
プレゼントをもらいっ放しって
わけにはいかないでしょ
だから、お礼にいいこと教えてあげる
speeches.English:
I can't just take a gift 
 and give nothing back. 
 Here's a tip to say thanks.

speeches.Japanese:
インドには素晴らしい建物があるの
ここまで来たなら
絶対に訪ねて損はないわ
speeches.English:
There's a magnificent building 
 in India. If you've come this far, 
 you really ought to see it.

speeches.Japanese:
ただ、地図がないとたどり着けないのが
難点なんだけど。ぜひ行ってみて
speeches.English:
You'll need a map to get there,
 though. You should really go 
 and see it.

speeches.Japanese:
ありがとう
地図を見つけたら行ってみるよ
speeches.English:
Thanks. If I find a map, I'll go 
 and see it.

SC0 B302.summary: Warns the party about the forest and offers directions if they bring a map

speeches.Japanese:
あら、FIさん
いらっしゃい
speeches.English: Oh, FI. Welcome.

speeches.Japanese:
遺跡ねえ…。この街の近くでは
聞いたことがないわね
speeches.English:
Ruins, huh? I've never heard of any
 near this town.

speeches.Japanese: じゃあ、もし遺跡を見つけたら…
speeches.English: So if we do find some ruins...

speeches.Japanese:
僕たちが第一発見者って
ことになるね！
speeches.English: We'd be the first ones to find them!

speeches.Japanese:
…そんなに簡単に見つからないわよ！
街の外はうっそうとした森だし
猛獣がうようよいて危険だわ
speeches.English:
...It won't be that easy!
 The forest outside town is thick,
 and it's full of dangerous animals.

speeches.Japanese:
それでも探検に出かけるつもりなら
内陸の方へ行く道を教えてあげる
でも、地図がないと森で道に迷うわよ
speeches.English:
If you're still set on exploring,
 I can show you the way inland. 
 But you'll get lost in the forest
 without a map.

SC0 B262.summary: Makes an exception for the travelers when she tells them about nearby ruins

speeches.Japanese:
あっFIさん
いらっしゃい！
speeches.English: Oh, FI! Welcome!

speeches.Japanese:
遺跡を探してるの？
この近くにもあるわよ
speeches.English:
Looking for ruins? There are some
 close by.

speeches.Japanese:
ホントは、異国の人には
教えないんだけど
特別に教えてあげる

SC0 B326.summary: Quietly shares directions to the city gate despite restrictions on visitors

speeches.Japanese:
FIさん
いらっしゃい
speeches.English: Ah, FI. Welcome.

speeches.Japanese: この街の城門の場所を知りたいの？
speeches.English:
You want to know where 
 the city gate is?

speeches.Japanese:
ほんとは外国の人に教えちゃ
いけないことになってるんだけど…
speeches.English:
I'm not really supposed
 to tell foreigners...

speeches.Japanese:
ま、外国の圧力のおかげで、この国の
鎖国なんてもう、あってないようなもの
だしね。いいわ
こっそり教えてあげる
speeches.English:
With all the pressure from abroad, 
 our policy of keeping the country
 closed is barely in effect anymore.
 All right. I'll tell you quietly.

SC0 B185.summary: Tells Rafael and Claudio what she heard about the crown and the earlier visitor

speeches.Japanese:
ねえ、クラウ
『新羅の金冠』のことを調べるには
どっから手をつけたらいいと思う？
speeches.English:
Hey, Clau. Where do you think
 we should start looking
 for the Silla Gold Crown?

speeches.Japanese:
そうだな
ちょっと聞いてみるか？
speeches.English: Hmm. Why don't we ask around?

speeches.Japanese: あら、いらっしゃい
speeches.English: Oh, welcome!

speeches.Japanese:
あんた『新羅の金冠』っての
知らねえか？
speeches.English: Ever heard of the Silla Gold Crown?

speeches.Japanese:
ええ、聞いたことはあるわ
それがどうかしたの？
speeches.English:
Yes, I've heard of it. 
 Why do you ask?

speeches.Japanese:
僕たち、それを探しているんです
知りませんか？
speeches.English:
We're looking for it. Do you know
 anything about it?

speeches.Japanese:
…ねえ、『新羅の金冠』を探すのが
今、流行ってるのかしら？
さっきも同じことを聞かれたんだけど
speeches.English:
Is the Silla Gold Crown in fashion?
 Someone just asked me about it.

speeches.Japanese:
それって…
調子のいい男だったか？
speeches.English: Was he... a bit of a smooth talker?

speeches.Japanese:
そうねえ。話を聞きたいのか
口説きたいのかって感じだったわね
speeches.English:
Well, I couldn't tell whether
 he wanted information or wanted
 to charm me.

speeches.Japanese:
ねえ、その人
ユリアンって名前じゃないですか？
僕たち、前に杭州で会ってるんです
speeches.English:
Was his name Julian, by any chance?
 We met him in Hangzhou.

speeches.Japanese:
そんな名前だったかしら…
よく覚えてないわ。ごめんなさい
でも、彼なら、『武寧王陵』に行った
みたい
speeches.English:
Was that his name? I'm sorry,
 I don't remember. I think he went
 to the Tomb of King Muryeong.

speeches.Japanese: 『武寧王陵』？
speeches.English: The Tomb of King Muryeong?

speeches.Japanese:
この近くにある遺跡よ
『新羅の金冠』はそこにあるって
話を聞いたことがあるの
speeches.English:
It's a historic site near here.
 They say you can find
 the Silla Gold Crown there.

speeches.Japanese:
おっと！　遅れを取っちまったな！
俺たちも急ごうぜ
FI！
speeches.English:
Uh-oh. He's ahead of us! Come on,
 FI, we'd better hurry!

SC0 B321.summary: Listens to Rafael’s travel story and asks about chintz

speeches.Japanese:
あっ、FIさん！
待ってたのよ！
speeches.English:
Oh, FI!
 I've been waiting for you!

speeches.Japanese:
ねえねえ
異国のお話、聞かせてくれる？
speeches.English:
Will you tell me about the places
 you've been?

speeches.Japanese:
ははは、分かった分かった
じゃあ、今日はインドの話を
聞かせてあげよう
speeches.English:
Ha ha! All right, all right. Today 
 I'll tell you about India.

speeches.Japanese:
へえ、インドってそんなに巨大な
動物がいるの！？
おもしろいわね！
speeches.English:
They have animals that big 
 in India? That's amazing!

speeches.Japanese:
インドで思い出したんだけど、とっても
きれいな更紗（サラサ）っていう
高級織物があるんですって？
speeches.English:
Speaking of India, 
 have you heard of chintz?
 A beautiful fabric, I hear.
 Expensive, too.

speeches.Japanese: 一度でいいから見てみたいなあ
speeches.English:
I'd love to see it for myself, 
 just once.

speeches.Japanese:
サラサか
今度買ったら見せてあげるよ
speeches.English:
Chintz, huh? Next time I buy some, 
 I'll show you.

speeches.Japanese: ホントね！？　楽しみに待ってるわ！
speeches.English: You promise? Oh, I can't wait!

SC0 B331.summary: Uses her improved fortune-telling to thank Rafael and point him toward ruins

speeches.Japanese: まあ、いらっしゃい！
speeches.English: Oh, welcome back!

speeches.Japanese:
あなたにもらった香炉のおかげで
占いがよく当たるようになったの
お礼に、あなたも占ってあげるわ
speeches.English:
My readings have been coming true
 more often thanks to that incense
 burner you gave me. Let me read
 your fortune to thank you.

speeches.Japanese: さ、そこに座って
speeches.English: Go on, have a seat right there.

speeches.Japanese:
この街からずっと内陸に行った
砂漠の奥に遺跡があるの。探している
物は、きっとそこにあるわ
speeches.English:
There are ruins deep in the desert,
 far inland. I'm sure you'll find 
 what you're looking for there.

SC0 B328.summary: Shares a report of an illustrated map but cannot say where it is

speeches.Japanese:
あ、FIさん
あなたに伝えなきゃと思って
すっかり忘れてたわ
speeches.English:
Oh, FI! I meant to tell
 you something, and it completely 
 slipped my mind.

speeches.Japanese:
この間、古代の絵地図が
見つかったんですって。それによると
この街の近くに古い王国の遺跡が
あるらしいの
speeches.English:
I heard someone found an ancient 
 illustrated map the other day. 
 It shows the ruins of an old 
 kingdom somewhere near this city.

speeches.Japanese:
へえ、絵地図かあ
それ、どこにあるの？
speeches.English: An illustrated map? Where is it?

speeches.Japanese:
ごめんなさい
そこまでは知らないんだけど
興味があるなら探しに行ってみたら？
speeches.English:
Sorry, I don't know that much. 
 If you're interested, why not go 
 look for it?

SC0 B335.summary: Asks the crew to inquire about a missing monk

speeches.Japanese: まあ、いらっしゃい
speeches.English: Oh, welcome!

speeches.Japanese:
ねえねえ
あなた、新大陸のずっと北にある村に
行ったことある？
speeches.English:
Ever visited a village way up north
 in the New World?

speeches.Japanese:
お客さんに聞いた話なんだけど
昔、この街の偉い修道士さんが
布教のために北の大陸に渡ったの
speeches.English:
A customer told me about 
 a respected monk from this city. 
 A long time ago, he sailed 
 to the northern continent
 to spread his faith.

speeches.Japanese:
その村を発見した後
行方不明になっちゃったんですって
何かあったのかしら？
speeches.English:
Apparently he went missing after 
 he found that village. I wonder
 what happened to him.

speeches.Japanese: さあ？
speeches.English: I don't know.

speeches.Japanese:
とても徳の高い人だったらしいの
布教先で慕われているといいんだけど
speeches.English:
He was supposed to be a very good
 man. I hope the people he went 
 to teach think fondly of him.

speeches.Japanese:
北に行く機会があったら
修道士さんの行方、聞いてみてね
speeches.English:
If you ever get a chance to go 
 north, would you ask around and see
 what became of him?

SC1 B115.summary: The follower cheers the leader, then cries out as the group is captured.

speeches.Japanese: むっ！
speeches.English: Hm?

speeches.Japanese: あああ～～～…
speeches.English: Aaaah...

speeches.Japanese: おおお～～～！
speeches.English: Ooooh!

speeches.Japanese:
歌でしょうか？
それにしても面妖な…
speeches.English: Is that singing? How strange...

speeches.Japanese:
これは、お告げなのだ！
我々『古代巨石文明研究会』は
近く、世界を制圧するであろう！
speeches.English:
It is a revelation! The Ancient
 Megalithic Civilization Research 
 Society will soon rule the world!

speeches.Japanese:
我々は選ばれし者！
ここに書かれた宝物を掘り出し
神をもおそれぬ愚民どもを
支配するのだ！！
speeches.English:
We are the chosen ones!
 We shall unearth the treasures 
 described here and rule
 those godless fools!

speeches.Japanese: おおーっ！
speeches.English: Ooooh!

speeches.Japanese:
……
穏やかではありませんな
speeches.English: ...Hardly peaceful.

speeches.Japanese:
まず手始めに、この村を襲う！
我々をばかにした連中に
思い知らせてやるのだ！
speeches.English:
We'll start by attacking 
 this village! We'll teach those who
 mocked us a lesson!

speeches.Japanese: おおおーっ！！
speeches.English: Ooooh!

speeches.Japanese:
……どうも、このまま捨て置くには
キナ臭すぎるな
speeches.English: This is too dangerous to ignore.

speeches.Japanese: すぐに村の住民を避難させましょう！
speeches.English: Get the villagers to safety at once!

speeches.Japanese:
よし、すぐに手配しろ
探検隊は総員戦闘準備にかかれ
speeches.English:
Good. See to it at once. The entire
 expedition is to prepare 
 for battle.

speeches.Japanese: はっ！
speeches.English: Yes!

speeches.Japanese:
火を放て！！
逆らう者は容赦するな！
speeches.English:
Set it ablaze! Show no mercy 
 to anyone who resists!

speeches.Japanese: おおう！
speeches.English: Ooh!

speeches.Japanese: ちょっと待った！
speeches.English: Wait!

speeches.Japanese: そこまでだ！！
speeches.English: That's enough!

speeches.Japanese:
観念しろ。今ならば、コトを穏便に
済ませてやってもいい
軍や国教会に裁かれるなど
本意ではなかろう？
speeches.English:
Surrender. We can still settle 
 this quietly. I doubt you want 
 to stand trial before the army 
 or the state church.

speeches.Japanese:
お、おのれ～、この私を裁くだと？
おそれを知らぬ愚か者どもめ！
一人残らず捕らえて、生け贄にせよ！
speeches.English:
Y-you dare judge me?! Insolent 
 fools! Capture every last one
 of them for sacrifice!

speeches.Japanese: おおーっ！！
speeches.English: Ooooh!

speeches.Japanese:
勇敢なのは認めるが
相手はよく見たほうがいい
speeches.English:
You're brave, I'll give you that.
 But take a good look at who
 you're facing.

speeches.Japanese:
さて
まずは、足もと注意、と
speeches.English: Now... mind your footing.

speeches.Japanese: うわあっ！！
speeches.English: Waaah!

speeches.Japanese:
はいはい
団体様、穴の底にご案内
speeches.English:
Right this way, everyone! Straight 
 to the bottom of the pit!

speeches.Japanese:
わ、罠だと！？
くそっ、何をやっておる！
こっちだっ！
speeches.English:
A t-trap?! Damn it! What 
 are you doing? Over here!

speeches.Japanese: おっと、そこも通行禁止だ
speeches.English: That way is closed too.

speeches.Japanese: いてっ、いたたた！！
speeches.English: Ow! Ow, ow!

speeches.Japanese: ほうら、引っかかった
speeches.English: Caught you!

speeches.Japanese: 捕縛しろ！
speeches.English: Bind them!

speeches.Japanese: わあああ！
speeches.English: Waaah!

speeches.Japanese:
……！！
一瞬のうちに百人近くいた
私のしもべたちが…
speeches.English:
Nearly a hundred of my followers...
 captured in an instant...

speeches.Japanese: き、貴様ら、何者だ！？
speeches.English: W-who are you?!

speeches.Japanese:
答える必要はなかろう
国軍の慈悲なき厳罰を希望した
おまえが知ったところで
仕方がないことだ
speeches.English:
I see no need to answer. You chose 
 the national army's merciless
 judgment. Knowing who we are won't 
 help you now.

speeches.Japanese: ん？　これは何だ？
speeches.English: Hm? What's this?

speeches.Japanese:
さ、触るな！　ああっ！
…お、終わりだ！
私の崇高なる使命が～あああ～！！
speeches.English:
D-don't touch that! No! It's over! 
 My glorious mission... Aaaah!

speeches.Japanese:
連行しろ
避難させた村人を帰還させたら
我々も引き上げるぞ
speeches.English:
Take them away. Once the evacuated 
 villagers are back, we'll
 withdraw too.

speeches.Japanese: はっ
speeches.English: Yes.

SC1 B259.summary: A follower interrupts the guildmaster to ask for a map, which connects the sect to the ruined site.

speeches.Japanese:
あ、ユリスさん
仕事を忘れて、今まで何してたんです？
領民がずいぶん困ってますよ
speeches.English:
Ah, Yuris. What have you been doing
 all this time, forgetting
 your duties? Your people 
 are in quite a bind.

speeches.Japanese:
すみませんねえ
遠出をすると、つい我を忘れて
しまって…。すぐに戻りますから
speeches.English:
I'm sorry. When I go on a long 
 trip, I get carried away 
 and lose track of everything...
 I'll go back at once.

speeches.Japanese:
本当にもう…。まあ、長旅で疲れてる
でしょうから、ここで一休みしてから
帰ってくださいよ
speeches.English:
Honestly... Rest here after
 your long journey, then go home.

speeches.Japanese:
おっと、忘れちゃいけねえ
これ、少ないけど礼金だ
取っといてくれ
speeches.English:
Almost forgot. 
 Take this small reward.

speeches.Japanese: 金貨１１０００枚を手に入れました
speeches.English: Received 11,000 gold coins.

speeches.Japanese:
ロンドンのシェアが
少し上がりました！
speeches.English:
Your market share in London
 increased slightly!

speeches.Japanese: おっと、ごめんよ。お客らしい
speeches.English:
Oh, excuse me. Looks like
 a customer.

speeches.Japanese: 親父、地図は売り切れか？
speeches.English: Hey, are you out of maps?

speeches.Japanese:
何だい。またあんたらか
ああ、もうねえよ
speeches.English: You again? Yeah, we're out.

speeches.Japanese: ちっ、使えん店だ
speeches.English: What a useless shop.

speeches.Japanese:
けっ、てめえらが
買い占めたんだろうが！
speeches.English: You're the ones who bought them all!

speeches.Japanese: 地図？
speeches.English: Maps?

speeches.Japanese:
遺跡への地図だよ
最近、妙な連中が入り浸ってて
近くの住民が迷惑してるらしい
speeches.English:
Maps to some ruins. A strange
 bunch has been hanging 
 around there lately, making
 a nuisance of themselves 
 with the people nearby.

speeches.Japanese: ここから近いのか？
speeches.English: Nearby?

speeches.Japanese:
かなり遠いんだが、地図があれば
簡単に行ける。ところが、地図は
みんなあの連中が
買ってっちまった
speeches.English:
They're quite far away,
 but with a map, they're easy 
 to reach. Trouble is, those people 
 bought every last one.

speeches.Japanese:
ほかの街には
まだあるかもしれないんだがね
speeches.English: Another town may still have one.

speeches.Japanese: なるほど…
speeches.English: Got it...

SC1 B295.summary: Teases Hodram and passes on a rumor about a hidden Christian village

speeches.Japanese: まあ、いらっしゃい
speeches.English: Well, welcome.

speeches.Japanese:
あなたって
よく見るとちょっといい男ね
いいこと教えてあげる
speeches.English:
You're rather handsome, now
 that I get a good look at you. 
 Let me give you a little tip.

speeches.Japanese:
この近くにキリスト教徒の隠れ里が
あるって話、聞いたことある？
speeches.English:
Have you heard of a hidden 
 Christian village nearby?

speeches.Japanese: 知らんな
speeches.English: No.

speeches.Japanese:
なんでも、岩をくり抜いて作った家に
住んでるらしいわ
あくまでも噂なんだけどね
speeches.English:
They supposedly live in houses 
 carved from rock.
 Only a rumor, though.

SC2 B106.summary: The follower echoes the Sect Leader as the ritual escalates and the villagers intervene.

speeches.Japanese: あっ、へんな祭りってあれかな？
speeches.English: So that's the odd festival?

speeches.Japanese: あああ～～～…
speeches.English: Aaaah...

speeches.Japanese: おおお～～～！
speeches.English: Ooooh!

speeches.Japanese:
う、歌？
ワインで酔っぱらってるのかな？
speeches.English: Singing? Are they drunk on wine?

speeches.Japanese: しっ！
speeches.English: Shh!

speeches.Japanese:
これは、お告げなのだ！
我々『古代巨石文明研究会』は
近く、世界を制圧するであろう！
speeches.English:
This is a revelation!
 Our Ancient Megalithic 
 Civilization Research Society
 shall soon rule the world!

speeches.Japanese:
我々は選ばれし者！
ここに書かれた宝物を掘り出し
神をもおそれぬ愚民どもを
支配するのだ！！
speeches.English:
We are the chosen ones!
 We shall unearth the treasure
 described here and rule
 those godless fools!

speeches.Japanese: おおーっ！
speeches.English: Ooooh!

speeches.Japanese: なんか…やだなあ…
speeches.English: This is creepy...

speeches.Japanese:
まず手始めに、この村を襲う！
我々をばかにした連中に
思い知らせてやるのだ！
speeches.English:
We attack this village first!
 Those who mocked us will pay!

speeches.Japanese: おおおーっ！！
speeches.English: Ooooh!

speeches.Japanese: な、なんですってえ！？
speeches.English: W-what?!

speeches.Japanese:
こらーっ！！
そんなこと、あたしが許さないわよ！！
speeches.English:
Hey! You won't hurt this village 
 on my watch!

speeches.Japanese: わっ、バカ！
speeches.English: You idiot!

speeches.Japanese: FI！！
speeches.English: FI!!

speeches.Japanese:
あそこにまだ神の意思に逆らう
者がおる…
引っ捕らえて、生け贄にせよ！！
speeches.English:
Someone over there still defies
 God's will... Seize them and make
 them a sacrifice!

speeches.Japanese: おおおう！
speeches.English: Ooooh!

speeches.Japanese: きゃあっ！
speeches.English: Eek!

speeches.Japanese: …ったく、このお嬢さんはよう！
speeches.English: That girl's a handful...

speeches.Japanese: 待てえっ！
speeches.English: Stop!

speeches.Japanese:
邪教徒め！
おぞましい行状は明らかだ！
もう、勝手にはさせん！
村の遺跡をわしらに返せ！
speeches.English:
Heretics! We know of your vile 
 deeds! We won't let
 you do as you please any longer. 
 Give our village's ruins back!

speeches.Japanese: うっ、くそっ！
speeches.English: Damn it!

speeches.Japanese: 村の人たち…？
speeches.English: The villagers?

speeches.Japanese:
来てくれたのね！
よかったー、近くの村に
声をかけておいて！
speeches.English:
You came! I'm so glad I told 
 the people in the nearby village!

speeches.Japanese:
こんなこともあろうかと思いまして
村の住民にも応援を頼んで
おいたのです
speeches.English:
I thought this might happen, 
 so I asked the villagers 
 for help, too.

speeches.Japanese:
こんなこともあるかと思ってよ
村の連中にも応援を頼んで
おいたんだ
speeches.English:
I had a feeling something
 like this might happen, so I asked 
 the villagers for help.

speeches.Japanese:
うぬぬ～、わしは逃げるぞ！！
むっ！！　ない！？
ないぞ！　どこだ！？
speeches.English:
Grr! I'm getting out of here!
 What?! It's gone! Where is it?!

speeches.Japanese:
これのことかい？
大事そうに祭壇に置いてあったから
ちょいと拝見させてもらってるよ
speeches.English:
You mean this? It looked 
 important sitting on the altar,
 so I'm just having a look.

speeches.Japanese:
さ、触るな！　ああっ！
…お、終わりだ！
私の崇高なる使命が～あああ～！！
speeches.English:
D-don't touch it! Aaah!
 It's all over! My noble
 mission... Aaaah!

speeches.Japanese: ほら！　おとなしくしろっ！！
speeches.English: Settle down!

speeches.Japanese:
ありがとうよ
あんたらが知らせてくれたおかげで
村が救われたよ
speeches.English:
Thank you. You saved our village 
 by warning us!

speeches.Japanese:
たいした礼もできんが
ロンドンまで送らせよう
あの森は熊が出るからな
speeches.English:
We can't offer much in thanks, 
 but we'll have you escorted
 to London. Bears roam those woods.

speeches.Japanese:
く、くまぁ？
もうコリゴリよ…
speeches.English: B-bears? No more, please...

speeches.Japanese:
心配せんでも、腕ききの猟師を
つけておくよ
気をつけてお帰り
speeches.English:
Don't worry. I'll send a skilled 
 hunter with you. Have a safe 
 journey home.

SC3 B88.summary: The follower cheers the Sect Leader and flees from what they mistake for the army.

speeches.English: Hm?!

speeches.Japanese: あああ～～～…
speeches.English: Aaaah...

speeches.Japanese: おおお～～～！
speeches.English: Ooooh!

speeches.Japanese: きっとあれね、妙な連中っていうのは
speeches.English: Those must be the strange people.

speeches.Japanese:
これは、お告げなのだ！
我々『古代巨石文明研究会』は
近く、世界を制圧するであろう！
speeches.English:
This is a revelation!
 We, the Ancient Megalithic 
 Civilization Research Society, 
 shall soon conquer the world!

speeches.Japanese:
我々は選ばれし者！
ここに書かれた宝物を掘り出し
神をもおそれぬ愚民どもを
支配するのだ！！
speeches.English:
We are the chosen! We'll unearth 
 the treasures recorded here
 and rule over those godless fools!

speeches.Japanese: おおーっ！
speeches.English: Ooooh!

speeches.Japanese: うむむ、狂っとる…
speeches.English: They're mad...

speeches.Japanese:
まず手始めに、この村を襲う！
我々をばかにした連中に
思い知らせてやるのだ！
speeches.English:
We begin by raiding this village!
 Those who mocked us will pay!

speeches.Japanese: おおおーっ！！
speeches.English: Ooooh!!

speeches.Japanese:
！！
…どうやら、とんでもない場面に
出くわしたようね
speeches.English: Oh! We've walked into a nightmare.

speeches.Japanese:
どうする、FI
強襲するには、銃が足りぬぞ
speeches.English:
What shall we do, FI? We haven't
 enough guns for an assault.

speeches.Japanese:
銃はあるだけでいいわ
空砲の準備を
speeches.English: Our guns will do. Load blanks.

speeches.Japanese: 空砲？
speeches.English: Blanks?

speeches.Japanese: それから、あれを使うわ。準備して
speeches.English: We'll use that, too. Get it ready.

speeches.Japanese: へい！
speeches.English: Yes!

speeches.Japanese:
それから、ジャム
あれを使うわ
speeches.English: Jam, use that too.

speeches.Japanese: イヤホウ！　お祭りだ！
speeches.English: Yahoo! A festival!

speeches.Japanese:
それから、シャルル
あれを使うわ
speeches.English: Charles, use that too.

speeches.Japanese:
え？
ああ、あれですね！
speeches.English: What? Ah, that!

speeches.Japanese:
火を放て！！
逆らう者は容赦するな！
speeches.English:
Set the fires! Show no mercy 
 to anyone who resists!

speeches.Japanese: おおう！
speeches.English: Ooooh!

speeches.Japanese:
邪教徒ども！！
教会より通告があった！
おとなしく投降しろ！！
speeches.English:
Heretics! We've received word
 from the church! 
 Surrender peacefully!

speeches.Japanese: 何者！？
speeches.English: Who are you!?

speeches.Japanese: 撃てい！！
speeches.English: Shoot!!

speeches.Japanese: ひっ！！
speeches.English: Eek!!

speeches.Japanese:
わあっ、国軍だ！！
逃げろーっ！
speeches.English: The army! Run away!

speeches.Japanese:
あ、こらっ、貴様ら！！
逃げるな！！
私を守らぬか！
speeches.English:
Stop, you fools! Don't run!
 Protect me!

speeches.Japanese:
軍が出てきたら、もうだめだ！
し、死にたくねえ！！
speeches.English:
We can't beat an army! D-don't 
 want to die!!

speeches.Japanese:
くそっ、何を言ってもだめだ！
ええい、臆病者どもめ！
speeches.English:
Damn! They won't listen! Cowards,
 all of them!

speeches.Japanese: あれを置いていくわけにはいかん！
speeches.English: Can't leave that behind!

speeches.Japanese: うっ！！
speeches.English: Ugh!!

speeches.Japanese: 何かしら、これ？
speeches.English: What's this?

speeches.Japanese:
さ、触るな！
返せ！　返さんか！！
speeches.English: D-don't touch it! Give it back!!

speeches.Japanese:
そのあわてようから察するに
よほど大事なもののようね
speeches.English:
Judging by your panic, 
 it must be very important.

speeches.Japanese: 貴様ぁ～！
speeches.English: You...!

speeches.Japanese:
あら、剣を使うの？
刃物の取り扱いには
気をつけたほうがいいわよ
speeches.English:
Oh, drawing your sword? Handle 
 sharp things with care.

speeches.Japanese: だまれっ！
speeches.English: Silence!

speeches.Japanese: ぐえっ！！
speeches.English: Gaaah!!

speeches.Japanese:
やんちゃな教祖じゃのう
これはきつーいお仕置きが必要じゃ
speeches.English:
Such a naughty cult leader.
 He needs a very stern lesson.

speeches.Japanese:
！？
な、なぜ、国軍に東洋人ばかりが
いるのだ？
speeches.English:
!? Wh-why is the army full 
 of Easterners?

speeches.Japanese:
国軍？
あなたの国の軍隊は
花火や爆竹なんかで敵と戦うの？
speeches.English:
The army? Does your country's army 
 fight its enemies with fireworks 
 and firecrackers?

speeches.Japanese: は、花火！！　爆竹だと～！？
speeches.English: F-fireworks!? Firecrackers!?

speeches.Japanese:
火薬は中国の発明品よ。西洋人のほうが
戦争にはうまく利用しているよう
だけれど
こういった用途はご存じないようね
speeches.English:
Gunpowder was invented 
 in China. Westerners 
 seem to have put 
 it to better use in war, 
 but apparently you don't know about
 uses like these.

speeches.Japanese: ぐぐぐ…！！
speeches.English: Grrr...!!

speeches.Japanese: 引き上げるわよ！
speeches.English: We're leaving!

review_scope: Default name and role decisions. Actual full list and conditional name consumers have separate display coverage.
